input: The pricing case considers a SaaS tier that is currently priced at $393 per unit, with a variable cost of $201 per unit and fixed costs of $265k per year. Subtracting the variable cost from the price gives a contribution of $192 per unit, which is the amount available from each sale to contribute towards the fixed costs of the business. On this basis, the break-even volume has been calculated at 1380 units per year, which is the level of sales at which total contribution exactly covers the fixed costs. Current volume, however, is only 822 units per year, which means that the tier is presently trading below its break-even level, with a shortfall of 558 units per year relative to the 1380 units required. It is important to note that the volume figures used in this analysis are last year's actuals, and the effect of the price on volume has not been estimated, so it cannot simply be assumed that a change in price would leave the sales volume unaffected. Increasing the price would raise the contribution per unit, but it might also reduce the volume achieved, and the overall impact on the position relative to break-even is therefore difficult to predict with confidence. This is a matter of some concern for the management of the tier, because the fixed costs of the business must be met from the contribution that is actually generated by the sales that are achieved, and at the present level of volume that contribution is not sufficient for the purpose, so that the tier is, in effect, being carried by the wider business while the shortfall persists.
target: Break-even volume for the SaaS tier is 1380 units per year, and current volume is 822 units per year, so the tier trades below break-even. The price is $393 per unit and the variable cost is $201 per unit, which gives a contribution of $192 per unit, derived as price less variable cost. Contribution is the amount each unit sold puts towards fixed costs after its variable cost is met, and break-even is the volume at which the accumulated contribution equals the fixed costs. Fixed costs are $265k per year, and the contribution from 1380 units covers them; the contribution from the current volume leaves a shortfall of 558 units against break-even. Volume figures are last year's actuals. Each term of the calculation is a lever of a different kind. Volume is a sales outcome. Variable cost is set by the cost of serving one more account. Fixed costs are committed for the year and do not move with volume. Price is the only lever management sets directly, and it is also the lever whose volume consequence the case does not estimate. The case therefore turns on volume growth at the stated price, or on a change in price, variable cost, or fixed costs. The effect of the price on volume is not estimated, and the case holds price and volume apart for that reason: a price change that raised the contribution per unit could also lower the volume, and the stated break-even would move in both terms at once. On last year's actuals, and with the price effect unestimated, the tier does not cover its fixed costs at the current volume.
